name: keepr.cloud_todo_change
about: The todo change protocol of supabase/migrations/20261118110000_backlog_4263_todo_server_core.sql (BACKLOG-4263): the ops cloud_todo_push and the core accept, the answers they give, and the rows cloud_todo_pull returns. Checked against the migration text by supabase/tests/backlog-4263/harness.py check.

push.function: cloud_todo_push(p_expected_user_id uuid, p_source_install_id uuid, p_sent_at text, p_ops jsonb)
push.effective_time: receive time - (p_sent_at - op.edited_at); -infinity (unknowable) when the age is below 0, above 365 days, either reading is missing or unparseable, or op.clock_stepped is true

pull.function: cloud_todo_pull(p_expected_user_id uuid, p_source_install_id uuid, p_after_seq bigint, p_limit integer, p_horizon bigint DEFAULT NULL)
pull.cursor: The desktop stores the pair (next_after, horizon) from every page it has applied, in the same local transaction as that page, and sends both back as p_after_seq and p_horizon. A full pull starts with p_after_seq 0 and p_horizon omitted (NULL) and keeps the horizon of each page it applies. p_after_seq > 0 without p_horizon answers {ok:false, error:'horizon_required'}. When resync_required is true the desktop applies nothing from that answer, drops its cursor and starts a full pull (p_after_seq 0, no p_horizon).
pull.resync_rule: resync_required = p_after_seq > head OR (p_after_seq > 0 AND forgotten_at > p_horizon AND forgotten_through_seq > p_after_seq). A cursor at or above forgotten_through_seq (caught up) never resyncs; a full pull from 0 never resyncs.
pull.horizon: horizon is the owner's forgotten_at marker read in the same snapshot as the page: a fresh number taken by every purge run that deletes anything, so it only moves forward. It is not a row number and is only compared with the horizon the desktop sends back.

ledger.rule: An op's answer is kept for exact replay unless it wrote nothing and can change without the op changing. A repeated op_id whose answer was kept returns that answer and writes nothing; a repeated op_id whose answer was not kept is evaluated again.

field_types.rule: A field present with a JSON type outside its list rejects that op alone (status rejected, reason invalid_value, field = the field names); the batch continues. op_id and kind are checked for the whole batch (invalid_input). edited_at of the wrong type or unparseable makes the op's time unknowable (E2).
title: string
field_types.value: per part (done boolean|{is_checked, checked_at}; title string; note string|null; due YYYY-MM-DD|null; order integer|null)

wire_types.rule: Every value is sent as the JSON type listed in field_types; the server does not convert. Booleans are JSON true/false (never 0/1 or strings). A set op's value is the bare part value, never wrapped in an object keyed by the part name. Times are ISO 8601 strings with a zone (for example 2026-11-17T04:05:08.266Z); due_date is a YYYY-MM-DD string; ids (id, deal_id, checklist_id) are uuid strings, compared as uuids in any letter case; a malformed uuid rejects the op with reason invalid_value, a final answer kept for replay (never not_found or parent_missing); local ids (local_id, checklist_local_id) are free text; integers are JSON numbers without a fraction.

examples_refused.why: part value wrapped by part name

my_items.mapped: create_checklist with template_id keepr:my-items answers status 'mapped' when the deal already has a live My items list online under another local id. The answer's cloud_id is that list. The server records the desktop's local_id as a name of that list (mapped_local_ids), so every later op from that desktop may keep naming it by its own local_id: create_item checklist_local_id, and set/restore on entity checklist by deal_id + local_id. A repeated create_checklist with that local_id answers 'mapped' again.
my_items.desktop_after_mapped: Store the answer's cloud_id as the cloud id of the local My items list (the shadow) and keep the local list. Send item creates with checklist_id = that cloud id, or with checklist_local_id = the desktop's own local id (both resolve). Ops already answered rejected/parent_missing are not kept in the ledger, so the same op_id can be sent again. Do not create a second list.
my_items.parent_resolution: create_item from the desktop names its parent by checklist_id (cloud uuid) or checklist_local_id (the list's local id or a local id answered 'mapped'); the parent must be a checklist of the op's deal, which must be this owner's and this install's. A parent on another deal or of another owner answers rejected/parent_missing.
my_items.list_removal: A keepr:my-items checklist is removed only with its deal: a remove op on it answers not_allowed for every actor. Its items are removed one by one. Reorder (set order) applies to the one online list.
